Signs of the World

Toxic material

History

In 1829, New York became the first US state to require labels on poisons, and the skull and crossbones appears to have been used for that purpose since the 1850s. Today the Globally Harmonized System for chemical labeling sets it in a red diamond, while the ISO 7010 safety standard uses a yellow triangle.

Adoption

The skull and crossbones warns of poison around the world. In the United States, concern that its pirate associations might attract children led to a green alternative, Mr. Yuk.
